system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: micro.AgentPrompt("You manage tasks and projects. You understand deadlines and priorities."),
system_prompt_style.note: Prompt supplied per-agent via option; tools/services discovered at runtime could make it dynamically composed.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The agent discovers its services from the registry, scopes its tools to their endpoints, and maintains conversation memory in the store.
env_context_strategy.note: Environment knowledge = service/tool schemas from registry; agent calls tools to act.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: older turns are collapsed into a deterministic summary, recent turns stay verbatim, and relevant archived turns are recalled on future asks
context_compaction.note: Opt-in via AgentCompactMemory(maxMessages, keepRecent); default memory is uncompacted.

observation_format.note: Tool calls/results are JSON over RPC; raw text also plausible but not directly evidenced.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Tools are services — endpoint metadata becomes tool schema; RPC executes the call.
tool_call_format.note: agent/text_tool_calls.go suggests a text fallback parser also ships.

tool_count.note: Tool count is dynamic (one per service endpoint) plus built-in plan and delegate; no fixed default count given.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Tools are your services automatically, plus any function you register with `AgentTool`.
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing primitive in the default agent tool set.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Doc comments and `@example` tags become tool descriptions for AI agents automatically.
tool_schema_source.note: Schemas derived from endpoint metadata; MCP gateway exposes them.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Interop is built in — MCP for tools, A2A for agents, x402 for paid tools.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: **`plan`** — for multi-step work, the agent records an ordered plan in its store-backed memory and stays oriented across turns.
loop_primitives.note: Default loop is tool-calling react with MaxSteps; plan tool built in; flows are event-driven.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the agent records an ordered plan in its store-backed memory and stays oriented across turns

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: the agent hands a self-contained subtask to another agent
multi_agent_topology.note: delegate is a built-in tool every agent gets.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: otherwise a focused, short-lived sub-agent is created for the subtask with its own isolated context

short_term_state.evidence_quote: the agent records an ordered plan in its store-backed memory and stays oriented across turns

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: **Memory** is durable and store-backed by default (Postgres, NATS KV, or file), so an agent picks up where it left off after a restart
long_term_memory.note: Store-backed conversation memory persisted across restarts.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Checkpointed flow steps survive a crash and resume where they stopped; store-backed by default, pluggable backend
state_persistence.note: Also examples/agent-durable: checkpoint and resume an agent run.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Safety lives at execution — `MaxSteps`, `LoopLimit`, `ApproveTool`, and tool wrappers run where actions happen.
self_verification.note: No harness-enforced tests, linters or judge on agent output documented.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: `AgentWrapTool` — wrap tool execution for logging, metrics, or retries (like client/server wrappers)
retry_policy.note: Retries only at tool/client level, not whole-task attempts.

rollback.evidence_quote: Checkpoint and resume an agent run without replaying completed tool side effects
rollback.note: No undo/revert of environment changes documented.

termination_condition.note: model_declared inferred from agent replying without tool calls.

cost_controls.note: ai/anthropic/cache_test.go indicates prompt caching; no token/cost budget documented.

timeouts.note: Guardrail list names no timeout; RPC-level timeouts likely but not evidenced here.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: An Agent is a service with an LLM inside it. It has a proto-defined `Agent.Chat` RPC endpoint
execution_isolation.note: Agent runs in-process in the Go service; tool calls execute via RPC to other services.

filesystem_access.note: No filesystem-access policy documented for the default agent (tools are RPC endpoints, not file ops).

network_policy.evidence_quote: Multiple agents coordinate via RPC — each is a service with an `Agent.Chat` endpoint.

permission_model.note: Approval is opt-in; by default tool calls execute unchecked. Agent tools are scoped to AgentServices endpoints.

tracing.note: OTel instrumentation ships in the agent package; default enablement not stated.

replayability.evidence_quote: Checkpoint and resume an agent run without replaying completed tool side effects

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: `make harness` runs the broader local contract
eval_hooks.note: CI/contract tests only; no benchmark evaluation runner shipped.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Safety lives at execution — `MaxSteps`, `LoopLimit`, `ApproveTool`, and tool wrappers run where actions happen.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Go Micro is an **agent harness** and service framework for Go.
target_domain.note: General tool use over services/MCP; swe via `micro run --prompt` service generation.

open_source.note: Apache-2.0 historically; license file present, text not quoted here.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: 9 LLM providers | Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, Mistral, Together, Atlas Cloud, MiniMax, Ollama (local + cloud)
